assumptions.value: The source evidence is remote object-storage Lance I/O.
The source run used one active payload reader on one physical node; all multi-reader and multi-node rates are queue-diagnostic extrapolations.
Minimum nodes needed to hold an evenly sharded index never choose the throughput profile; throughput node counts are explicit.
Payload reads equal image references, modeling no reuse across streaming windows. This is an upper-bound policy, not measured current-MINT I/O.
Logical-byte, physical-byte, and physical-call rates come from the same repeats. Their dominant arithmetic term does not prove storage saturation.
Runtime excludes scheduler startup, skew, retries, spill, output writes, object-store throttling changes, and failures.

evidence_legend.modeled: Arithmetic using explicit assumptions; not benchmark evidence.
evidence_legend.queue_diagnostic_extrapolation: Projected from one active reader; not a saturated per-node rate or SLA.

index_capacity.note: Index-memory capacity is independent of throughput provisioning. Even sharding and linear setup are architecture assumptions, not benchmark results.
